questions.question: Which statement correctly describes an electrophile? Options: A accepts a pair of electrons; B always negative; C always positive; D donates a pair of electrons.
questions.answer: A (accepts a pair of electrons)
steps: An electrophile is an electron-pair acceptor, so it is attracted to electron-rich sites.
B is wrong: electrophiles can be neutral (e.g. BF3) or positive, not always negative.
C is wrong: electrophiles are not always positive, since BF3 is neutral.
D describes a nucleophile, which donates a lone pair, so it is wrong.
Answer A.

questions.question: For the process H2O -> H+ + OH-, what type of bond breaking occurs? Options: A electrophilic; B heterolytic; C homolytic; D ionic.
questions.answer: B (heterolytic)
steps: In H2O -> H+ + OH-, the O-H bond breaks and forms ions.
Both electrons of the bond go to the oxygen atom, leaving H+ with none.
When one atom takes both electrons of the bond, the fission is heterolytic.
Homolytic fission gives radicals, not ions, and electrophilic and ionic are not types of bond breaking here.
Answer B.

questions.answer: B (homologous series)
steps: Consecutive members of the sequence differ by one CH2 unit.

questions.question: Write a balanced equation for the thermal decomposition of (NH4)2Cr2O7 at about 180 deg C, giving an oxide of chromium, nitrogen and water as the only products.
questions.answer: (NH4)2Cr2O7 -> Cr2O3 + N2 + 4H2O
steps: Products are Cr2O3 (oxide of chromium), N2 (nitrogen) and H2O (water).
N: 2 on the left, so 1 N2 on the right.
Cr: 2 on the left, so 1 Cr2O3 on the right.
H: 8 on the left, so 4 H2O on the right (4 x 2 = 8 H).
O: 7 on the left (7 O in the salt), and 3 + 4 = 7 on the right, so the equation balances.

questions.question: Give a name for the type of reaction in part (a)(i).
questions.answer: Thermal decomposition (it is also a redox reaction)
steps: One compound breaks down into simpler products when heated, which is thermal decomposition.
Cr falls from +6 to +3 in Cr2O3, so it is reduced.
N rises from -3 in NH4+ to 0 in N2, so it is oxidised.
The reaction is therefore also a redox reaction.

questions.question: 0.00100 mol of (NH4)2Cr2O7 is heated and 25.2 cm^3 of N2 is formed at laboratory temperature. Using pressure 101 kPa and PV = nRT, find the laboratory temperature in deg C.
questions.answer: About 33 deg C (about 306 K)
steps: From the equation, 1 mol of (NH4)2Cr2O7 gives 1 mol of N2, so n(N2) = 0.00100 mol.
Convert pressure: 101 kPa = 101000 Pa.
Convert to Celsius: 306 - 273 = 33 deg C.

questions.question: Draw a dot-and-cross diagram of the ammonium ion, using dots for nitrogen electrons and crosses for hydrogen electrons.
questions.answer: Nitrogen at the centre with four N-H single bonds; each bond is one shared pair (one dot from N, one cross from H); no lone pair on N; whole ion in square brackets with +.
steps: Nitrogen has 5 outer electrons and each hydrogen has 1, so the total is 9, and the +1 charge removes one, leaving 8.
Those 8 electrons form four N-H bonds, so there are four shared pairs.
Each bond is shown as one dot (from N) and one cross (from H).
N has no lone pair in NH4+, so there are no extra dots on nitrogen.
Enclose the ion in square brackets and write + at the top right.

questions.question: Explain the shape of the ammonium ion using electron-pair repulsion theory.
questions.answer: Tetrahedral: four bonding pairs and no lone pairs repel equally, giving bond angles of 109.5 deg.
steps: The central N atom has four bonding pairs of electrons and no lone pairs.
Electron pairs repel each other and move as far apart as possible to minimise repulsion.
Four equal repulsions give a tetrahedral arrangement.
The H-N-H bond angles are 109.5 deg.

questions.question: What do heterolytic fission products consist of? Options: A free radicals only; B ions only; C free radicals and positive ions only; D free radicals and negative ions only.
questions.answer: B (ions only)
steps: Heterolytic fission: both electrons of the bond go to one atom.
This gives a positive ion (cation) and a negative ion (anion).
Free radicals form only in homolytic fission, where each atom gets one electron.
So heterolytic fission produces ions only, answer B.

questions.question: In an experiment using hydrogen peroxide to measure rate of decomposition, which of these reduce the risk: (I) an alternative method with less hazardous materials, (II) working on a smaller scale, (III) taking precautions specific to the hazard? Options: A (I) only; B (III) only; C (II) and (III); D (I), (II) and (III).
questions.answer: D ((I), (II) and (III))
steps: (I) An alternative method with less hazardous materials removes the hazard at source.
(II) A smaller scale reduces the amount of hazardous material used and the exposure risk.
(III) Precautions specific to the hazard, such as eye protection, reduce the risk directly.
All three reduce risk, so the answer is D.
